long_biography.plain_text:
George Melissanidis learned shipping through maritime studies and work aboard company vessels. When he became Aegean Shipping's chairman in 2007, he took responsibility for an established family-controlled management business rather than a start-up of his own. His role has been operational and strategic, while professional chief executives supervise daily management.

Under Melissanidis, Aegean replaced older tankers with newly built, more efficient ships and entered dry-bulk transport through Aegean Eco Carriers. It also introduced paperless operations, formal business-continuity systems and sustainability-linked financing. Melissanidis owns the shipping business, but its vessels and financing arrangements remain assets of companies or vessel-owning principals, not his individually titled property.

It does not disclose the exact date, legal instrument or consideration by which ownership passed to him. Marriage / family transfer is therefore used above the acceptance threshold but below very-high confidence; inherited is avoided because the senior generation remains living.

The wider Melissanidis family has documented oil, marine-fuel and environmental businesses, but neutral public sources do not establish that George personally owns or principally derives wealth from all of them. His classification is confined to the directly evidenced Aegean Shipping platform.

Trade sources call Aegean Shipping George's company, but the corporate site distinguishes management entities, Aegean Eco Carriers and vessel-owning principals. Fleets, individual vessels, loans, sale proceeds and charter income are therefore treated as company or principal assets, not automatically as his individually titled property.
